short: Government troops slaughtered thirty-eight members of Clan MacDonald in their own homes.
full:
On the morning of 13 February 1692, government soldiers quartered in the Scottish Highlands turned on their hosts, the MacDonalds of Glencoe. The clan chief had been late in swearing a required oath of allegiance to William III, providing the government with a pretext to make an example of them. Acting on strict orders, the troops killed thirty-eight men, women and children.

The breach of hospitality, a grave offence in Highland culture, shocked Scottish society and fueled deep resentment. The massacre became a powerful piece of Jacobite propaganda, cementing Highland opposition to the new regime and ensuring lingering hostility towards the Campbell clan, whose members had commanded the attacking forces.
